items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: nobody really realized how good a piano player Count Basie was in his early days, he was a terror if you listen to the Bennie Moten things from 1932 on.

ctx.x: You know, ‘cause taste is above all the arbiter of greatness I think. Count Basie was – nobody really realized how good a piano player Count Basie was in his early days, he was a terror if you listen to the Bennie Moten things from 1932 on. He played more damn piano than Fats on those records, which is really saying something and never did with his own band that much piano. But the man had such great taste that those few ideas he used to throw around, that if anybody else did you’d be sick of him within a few…
Yeah, Mel was like that too.
